objective: FARO STUDIO PLAYBOOK 07 — Backend-Enabled Ideation: scan trends, brainstorm 5+ concepts that leverage a back-end server (multi-user, real-time, cloud sync, hosted AI, community), and score them. Read-only. Produces a ranked shortlist for the Director to fund.

steps.task: Scan for trends where a BACK-END SERVER creates the market opportunity or is the key differentiator. Read products/<slug>/BRIEF.md and any products/ideas/ notes first. Focus on: real-time collaboration, multi-user/social, cloud sync, hosted AI/ML services, community/UGC, cross-device continuity, and server-side data aggregation. If web research tools are not granted, work from local evidence only and mark items needing verification. Produce: trend table (name, source/date, platform, confidence, product implication), opportunity gaps ranked by ease-of-exploitation × market-impact, and 'why now' analysis for each.

Using trend-scan evidence and the product brief, generate 5+ distinct product concepts that REQUIRES or strongly benefits from a back-end server. Each concept must: have a unique angle (not a clone), address a real user frustration from the evidence, and clearly justify the server (e.g., multi-user collaboration, real-time sync, hosted AI, community content, cross-device presence). Return: concept name, one-line pitch, target user fantasy, core mechanic/interaction, server-side features, emotional arc, visual mood, 'why now', estimated complexity (client + backend). Rank by novelty × feasibility × emotional impact.

Review every concept from the ideate lane from a game-design perspective. For concepts that include game mechanics or gamification elements, evaluate: core loop viability, session length targets, retention hooks, difficulty curve plausibility, and economy feasibility (note which elements require the server). For non-game concepts, simply confirm they are not games and return 'N/A — non-game concept'. Return per-concept verdict: GAME-VIABLE / GAME-REQUIRES-WORK / NOT-A-GAME, with specific design notes for game-viable concepts.

Score every concept from the ideate lane 1-5 across: Novelty, Feasibility, Market Size, Differentiation, Store-Risk, Effort. Incorporate game-design-check verdicts. CRITICAL: for each concept, assess backend cost vs. user value (hosting, bandwidth, moderation, AI inference costs) and flag concepts where server cost undermines the business model. Produce a weighted composite score. Identify kill criteria: any concept whose server cost exceeds plausible revenue, that violates store policies, or that clones existing products gets NO-GO with the specific reason. Return: scoring matrix, top 3 recommendations with rationale, kill list with reasons, risk register for recommended concepts.

Reduce all lanes into the Director's ideation memo: ranked concept list (5+ concepts with scores), top 3 recommendations each with 'why fund this' and 'what to watch', kill list with reasons, and the exact next playbook to run for each funded concept (graphs/01-discovery.json for full Discovery). Include a specific note on backend architecture implications for each funded concept. Always respond in English.
